<reason>A genuinely tight, high-quality exchange. CON built a coherent mechanistic case (aggression at scale = automation = regressive false positives on invested players) and landed a sharp turn on PRO's triage answer ("cheap means automated; that middle is where my false positives live"). But PRO did more to make the motion decidable. PRO's "softer clothing" argument stuck: CON's own toolkit (default-off voice, quarantine-by-report, phone gates) is platform intervention that culture-objectors would resist and CON would override, so the contested clause is conceded in principle; CON's "a setting isn't a verdict" reply is thinner than it sounds, and CON quietly retreated from "quarantine the reported" to "quarantine new accounts" under that pressure. PRO's cost-shifting point (she mutes, she goes silent, he keeps the next lobby) was never squarely neutralized, and the "normative, not invoice" move partially defused CON's staffing arithmetic. PRO's closing weighing—veteran has an appeal, the girl's exit is silent—gave a cleaner reason to vote. CON also exceeded the cap three times versus PRO's once, a real execution cost. Clear but competitive win for PRO.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B2.1–B2.4 (PRO R1) reframing "aggressive" as investment rather than automation and turning CON's own tools into "aggressive moderation under a gentler name," which forced CON onto the defensive definitional ground it never fully escaped; CON's counter in A4.5–A4.6 (triage maps my case) was the strongest single reply but did not undo the concession-of-principle point.</best_rebuttal>
